meta.task: A35/M2-delta Tasks 2+3 -- (W-prime) queue re-collapse and sampled v2 certificate re-derivation
meta.sign_discipline: aux and dominance rows are ordinary g >= 0 rows: in FJ stationarity they carry lambda >= 0 and ADD generators (more sets can be cone-alive); in the escape-cone test they are constraints grad g . v >= 0 and STRICTLY SHRINK every escape cone (more sets are wedge-dead).  Both measured below.

effect1_note: If Z0 becomes ALL rows then every break set in the 2^42 lattice is cone-alive and the cone test kills nothing at all -- the aliveness expansion is total.  That is the price of the aux rows on the FJ side, and it is exactly compensated on the value side: the same aux rows restore a strictly positive uniform multiplier floor (m2b_global.json), which certifies every stratum at once.

vprime_coverage.why: m2b_global.py certifies, per (variant, selection), a single omega with A_ext^T omega = e_s and omega_r >= alpha_min > 0 on EVERY v2 row of the variant and on both aux rows.  The (V-prime) hypothesis (omega_b >= alpha_min for broken b, omega free on maintained rows) then holds for ANY break set B, so the certificate is stratum-INDEPENDENT and covers the whole 2^42 lattice, the (W-prime) survivors included.

task3_sampled_rederivation.note: a per-stratum certificate is the FULL tie menu (32 selections for selx/sely, 64 for conj); the stratum is only certified when every selection is, so secs_*_full_menu is the honest per-stratum price.  m2b_global.json prices the same coverage at 128 certificates for the ENTIRE lattice, so per-stratum re-derivation is never the right way to pay for this queue.
